data.title: Finding Angles Formed by Transversals
data.description: Practice finding unknown angle measures using the geometric relationships formed when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.

challenges.narration: A roof truss forms a triangle.
challenges.instruction: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Two are given — find the third, x.
challenges.hint: The angles of any triangle add to 180°, so x = 180° − the two known angles.

challenges.narration: A triangular sail forms a triangle.
challenges.instruction: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Two are given — find the third, x.
challenges.hint: The angles of any triangle add to 180°, so x = 180° − the two known angles.

challenges.narration: A ladder leaning across two shelves — two parallel lines cut by a transversal.
challenges.instruction: The marked angle and x are corresponding angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: corresponding angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel, so x equals the marked angle.

challenges.narration: A ladder leaning across two shelves — two parallel lines cut by a transversal.
challenges.instruction: The marked angle and x are alternate interior angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: alternate interior angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel, so x equals the marked angle.

challenges.narration: A yield sign has one side extended past a corner.
challenges.instruction: The exterior angle x equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.
